# The herdr mod gallery: large files and removal (2026-11-19)

Two questions from the `desktop-chat` proposal: does the gallery take a mod
that ships a large generated file, and can an entry be taken down again?
Method: every public repository tagged `herdr-mod` (886) and `herdr-layout`
(515) from GitHub's topic search, each repository's file tree through the
GitHub API, and the herdr.dev/mods page as served that day (718 linked
repositories).

## Large generated files are common and listed

36 tagged repositories hold a JavaScript or wasm file over 200 KB; in 32 it
sits inside a `mods/` folder, so a gallery install copies it. All of these
checked were listed on herdr.dev:

| Repository | Largest file in a mod folder | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| lukachi/openGPUI | 6.2 MB `opengpui.mjs`, 3.5 MB `shared.js` | a release build; its RECIPE says "build it from the source instead" |
| Calonca/herdr-wasm-mods | 2.7 MB `diff.wasm` | wasm run by a native host binary (below) |
| linziyanleo/herdr-mods | 1.6 MB `mermaid.bundle.js` | an esbuild bundle; the RECIPE gives the rebuild command and a `--check` that compares the generated bytes |
| CiprianSpiridon/herdr-mission-control | 0.8 MB `backend.mjs` | a bundled backend |

So a ~1 MB `core.js` is well within what the gallery already carries, and
openGPUI's RECIPE is a working precedent for "these files are one build;
rebuild from the source repository". Confidence: high that such entries are
listed; unknown how often installs of them succeed (not observable).

## Entries outlive their repositories

20 repositories linked from herdr.dev no longer turned up in the topic
search. Of these, 10 return 404 (deleted) and 2 exist with no gallery topic,
yet all were still listed. One is named `herdr-crawl-probe`: someone else's
test entry, archived and still listed. Removing the topic or deleting the
repository does not reliably take an entry down (how long it lingers is not
known). Confidence: moderate-high.

**Consequence:** no throwaway test listing. The first listing is the real
one, made only when the mod is ready.

## Notes for the build

- openGPUI's RECIPE: "Every pane of the mod shares one script engine with
  all mods": a slow `core.js` call stalls other mods too, and a trap in a
  shared engine is a reason for D10's whole-module reload.
- herdr-wasm-mods does not run wasm in QuickJS: its mods start a native
  "WASM Mods host" pinned in `host.lock.json` (URL and SHA-256 per platform,
  Linux and macOS only, downloaded or built from source on first use). It is
  a precedent for the helper-program fallback (decision 7), and shows that
  route also has no Windows build there.
- preview-plus's byte-compare `--check` of its generated bundle is worth
  copying for `core.js` in CI.
